basic_information.name: AGENTS.md
basic_information.creator: OpenAI (collaboratively developed with contributions from Amp, Cursor, Factory, Google Jules; donated to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation in December 2025, co-founded with Anthropic and Block)
basic_information.release_date: August 19, 2025 (GitHub repository created August 19, 2025; InfoQ coverage August 2025; donated to AAIF December 9, 2025)
basic_information.current_version: No formal versioned releases as of February 2026. The specification is a living Markdown document with no semantic versioning. A v1.1 proposal (Issue #135 on GitHub) has been submitted to formalize implicit semantics and clarify scope, but no official version tags exist on the repository.

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: Not applicable — AGENTS.md is not a framework or runtime. It is a documentation standard (a convention for a Markdown file placed in repositories). It defines no execution model, no code paths, and no architecture patterns. It is consumed by coding agents as static text context during their planning and execution phases.
technical_architecture.underlying_models: Model-agnostic by design. AGENTS.md is a plain Markdown file read by any AI coding agent regardless of the underlying LLM. Supported by agents built on: OpenAI GPT-4o/o1/o3 (Codex, Copilot), Anthropic Claude (Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md but not AGENTS.md natively; Copilot reads both), Google Gemini (Gemini CLI, Jules, Android Studio), and models powering Cursor, Devin, Aider, Windsurf, RooCode, Kilo Code, and others. The standard intentionally has zero model dependency.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: AGENTS.md does not integrate with tools directly. It is a documentation file that DESCRIBES tool usage to agents. Common content includes: which build tools to use (npm, make, cargo), which test runners to invoke, which linters to apply, which deployment commands to run. Agents consuming AGENTS.md then use their own tool-calling mechanisms (MCP, function calling, shell execution) to act on these instructions. AGENTS.md is complementary to MCP: AGENTS.md tells the agent WHAT to do, MCP tells it HOW to connect to tools.
technical_architecture.planning_approach: Not applicable — AGENTS.md is a static file, not a planning system. However, it significantly influences agent planning by providing: (1) explicit task boundaries and constraints, (2) step-by-step workflows for build/test/deploy, (3) coding conventions that guide code generation decisions, (4) pull request guidelines that shape how agents structure their output. The instructions in AGENTS.md effectively serve as 'planning constraints' that agents incorporate into whatever planning approach they use (ReAct, tree-of-thought, etc.).
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: AGENTS.md supports multi-agent scenarios through its hierarchical file structure. In monorepos, different nested AGENTS.md files can provide specialized instructions for different agents or subprojects. GitHub Copilot supports role-based agents defined via AGENTS.md frontmatter (e.g., @docs-agent, @test-agent, @security-agent), each with distinct personas and tool permissions. The standard itself does not orchestrate agents but provides the instruction layer that orchestrators consume.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: semantic (knowledge) — AGENTS.md files serve as static semantic memory for coding agents: a persistent, project-specific knowledge base that agents load at the start of each session. The file contains institutional knowledge about the project: architecture decisions, coding conventions, build workflows, and constraints. It does not support episodic, procedural, or short-term memory. Memory management beyond reading AGENTS.md is handled by the consuming agent framework.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: AGENTS.md influences context management but does not implement it. The specification's advice to keep files concise and well-structured helps agents parse relevant information efficiently. GitHub's analysis of 2,500+ repositories recommends: frontloading critical commands, using clear headings for section-based retrieval, and keeping the file focused to avoid wasting context window tokens. Agents typically load the nearest AGENTS.md content into their system prompt or context, with hierarchical merging from root to current directory.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: file_system — AGENTS.md is a plain text file persisted in the repository's filesystem, typically committed to version control (Git). It requires no database, vector store, or cloud service. Changes are tracked through standard Git history. The file is loaded fresh at the start of each agent session from the local filesystem.
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: AGENTS.md is itself a context engineering artifact. It treats project context as a first-class concern by providing a dedicated, standardized file that agents know to look for. The hierarchical discovery mechanism (root AGENTS.md merged with subdirectory-level files) enables layered context: global project conventions at root, package-specific guidance in subdirectories. AGENTS.override.md files allow local customization without modifying shared instructions. This approach ensures that every agent session starts with consistent, curated project context.

capabilities.core_capabilities: AGENTS.md provides a standardized, portable format for project-specific agent instructions. Core capabilities include: (1) Hierarchical file discovery — agents walk the directory tree from project root to working directory, loading and merging AGENTS.md files at each level, providing both global and local context. (2) Override mechanism — AGENTS.override.md files take precedence over AGENTS.md at the same directory level, enabling local customization (e.g., for personal preferences or environment-specific settings) without modifying shared instructions. (3) Monorepo support — nested AGENTS.md files provide package-level or module-level guidance in large repositories, ensuring agents receive tailored instructions regardless of which subdirectory they operate in. (4) Agent-agnostic format — plain Markdown with no required structure or fields, consumed by 20+ different AI coding agents. (5) Role-based agent personas (GitHub Copilot extension) — frontmatter-defined agents like @docs-agent, @test-agent, @security-agent with distinct instructions. (6) Content categories — build commands, test workflows, code style conventions, architecture documentation, security considerations, PR guidelines, and project structure descriptions. (7) Portability — same file works across Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Jules, Devin, Aider, Windsurf, Factory, and others.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Text only — AGENTS.md is a plain Markdown file. It supports standard Markdown formatting (headings, lists, code blocks, links, tables). It does not support images, audio, video, or other binary content. The text content instructs agents about how to handle code, files, terminal commands, and other modalities.
capabilities.autonomy_level: Not applicable — AGENTS.md is a documentation standard, not an agent. It influences agent autonomy by defining: (1) boundaries and restrictions (what the agent should NOT do), (2) approval requirements for certain actions, (3) command execution permissions. The actual autonomy level depends on the consuming agent. For example, an AGENTS.md file might instruct an agent to always run tests before committing (supervised pattern) or to never push to main without review (approval_required pattern).
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: AGENTS.md is consumed by 20+ AI coding agents and tools: OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot (coding agent), Cursor, Devin (Cognition), Google Gemini CLI, Google Jules, Google Android Studio (Gemini), Aider, Factory, Amp, Windsurf (Cognition), RooCode, Kilo Code, Phoenix, opencode, goose (Block), Zed, Warp, VS Code extensions, UiPath Autopilot & Coded Agents, Semgrep. The standard integrates with any Markdown-capable agent by convention — no plugin or SDK required.

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: AGENTS.md and MCP are complementary sibling projects under the Agentic AI Foundation. AGENTS.md provides the 'what to do' layer (project instructions, conventions, workflows), while MCP provides the 'how to connect' layer (tool and data connectivity). An agent might read AGENTS.md to learn it should run 'npm test' before committing, then use MCP to execute that command through a terminal server. Both were founding contributions to the AAIF in December 2025.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: No direct relationship. AGENTS.md is a documentation standard for single-agent project guidance, not a communication protocol. A2A (Agent-to-Agent Protocol by Google) handles inter-agent communication. AGENTS.md could contain instructions about how an agent should interact with other agents in a multi-agent setup, but it does not implement or support A2A directly.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: AGENTS.md IS the standard. It defines the convention for project-specific agent instruction files. All agents that support AGENTS.md read and respect its contents. Notable exception: Anthropic's Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md (its own proprietary format) rather than AGENTS.md natively, though GitHub Copilot reads both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. The recommended best practice when using Claude Code is to maintain both files, with CLAUDE.md referencing or including AGENTS.md content.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: Extremely high — AGENTS.md was designed from the outset as a cross-framework, cross-tool standard. Its use of plain Markdown with no required structure means any agent that can read text files can consume it. Supported by agents from OpenAI, Google, GitHub, Cognition, Cursor, and dozens of independent tools. The donation to the Linux Foundation's AAIF ensures vendor-neutral governance. The only significant gap is Anthropic's Claude Code, which uses CLAUDE.md instead (though other Anthropic-powered tools like Copilot do read AGENTS.md). The GitHub Blog analysis of 2,500+ repos confirms broad real-world cross-tool adoption.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: AGENTS.md itself has no enforcement mechanism — it is advisory text, not executable policy. However, it serves as a soft permission model: agents are instructed about what they may and may not do (e.g., 'never modify production configs', 'always run tests before committing', 'do not delete files without confirmation'). The actual enforcement depends on the consuming agent's implementation. Some agents (like Codex) treat AGENTS.md instructions as binding constraints; others may treat them as suggestions.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: AGENTS.md can define escalation policies in prose (e.g., 'if tests fail, stop and ask the developer', 'never force-push without human approval'). The standard itself does not enforce escalation — it documents the expected behavior. Agents like Codex and Copilot respect these instructions as part of their system prompt, effectively implementing the documented escalation policy.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: AGENTS.md helps mitigate agent hallucinations about project conventions by providing authoritative, project-specific ground truth. Without AGENTS.md, agents must guess build commands, coding styles, and workflows — leading to hallucinated or incorrect instructions. With AGENTS.md, agents have a verified reference. However, AGENTS.md introduces a new risk: prompt injection via malicious AGENTS.md files in untrusted repositories. If a developer clones a repo with a crafted AGENTS.md, the file could instruct the agent to perform unintended actions. This is an active security concern in the community.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: No built-in audit trail — AGENTS.md is a static file. However, changes to AGENTS.md are tracked through Git version control history, providing an audit trail of instruction modifications. The consuming agent's audit capabilities (logging, tracing) determine whether compliance with AGENTS.md instructions is tracked.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: AGENTS.md enables any human oversight pattern through documentation: it can instruct agents to require pre-approval for destructive actions, to always include human review before merging, or to operate autonomously within defined boundaries. The pattern is not enforced by the standard — it is communicated through prose instructions that well-behaved agents follow. The hierarchical override mechanism (AGENTS.override.md) lets individual developers add personal oversight preferences.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), a directed fund under the Linux Foundation (established December 9, 2025). AGENTS.md was contributed by OpenAI as one of three founding projects alongside MCP (Anthropic) and goose (Block). Platinum members: Amazon Web Services, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI. The AAIF provides vendor-neutral governance for the standard's evolution.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: AGENTS.md is itself an open standard contributed to the AAIF. It complements: (1) MCP (Model Context Protocol) — for agent-to-tool connectivity, (2) goose (Block) — an open-source AI developer agent, (3) The broader AAIF ecosystem for agentic AI interoperability. AGENTS.md draws on existing conventions: README.md (human-facing project documentation), .editorconfig (editor settings), .github/CONTRIBUTING.md (contribution guidelines). It creates a new category: agent-facing project documentation.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: No direct regulatory compliance — AGENTS.md is a documentation convention, not a software service. However, AGENTS.md can support compliance by: (1) documenting required security practices for agents (no credential exposure, no unauthorized data access), (2) defining boundaries that align with regulatory requirements (e.g., 'never process PII outside approved systems'), (3) providing auditable instructions for how AI agents should behave in regulated environments. EU AI Act, SOC2, HIPAA compliance depends entirely on the agent implementation and the instructions codified in AGENTS.md, not the standard itself. [uncertain]

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: local | cloud — AGENTS.md is a plain text file that lives in the repository. It is 'deployed' by committing it to a Git repository. It works with: (1) local agent setups (Codex CLI, Cursor, VS Code), (2) cloud-based agents (GitHub Copilot coding agent, Google Jules, Devin), (3) any hybrid setup. The file itself has zero infrastructure requirements — no servers, no databases, no runtime.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: Not applicable — AGENTS.md is a static file, not a running system. It 'scales' through Git: every clone of the repository includes the file. In monorepos, the hierarchical file structure scales to arbitrarily large projects (OpenAI's own Codex repository has 88 AGENTS.md files). No compute or infrastructure scaling concerns.
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Zero direct cost. AGENTS.md is a free, open standard. Creating and maintaining the file is a documentation task, not a compute task. Indirect cost: the file's content consumes tokens in the agent's context window, which may marginally increase LLM API costs per request (typically a few hundred to a few thousand tokens, costing fractions of a cent per session). The ROI is strongly positive: GitHub's analysis shows that well-crafted AGENTS.md files significantly improve agent task success rates.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Near-zero. AGENTS.md requires: (1) a text editor to create, (2) a Git repository to store, (3) an AI coding agent to consume. No compute, no memory, no GPU, no network infrastructure. File size is typically 1-10 KB of Markdown text. The standard is deliberately designed to be as lightweight as possible.

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: No built-in monitoring — AGENTS.md is a static file. Observability of whether agents correctly follow AGENTS.md instructions depends on the agent's own monitoring stack (e.g., LangSmith for LangChain-based agents, Langfuse for open-source tracing, Datadog for enterprise monitoring). Some teams implement CI checks to validate that agent-generated code conforms to AGENTS.md guidelines (linting rules, test coverage requirements).
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: No built-in tracing. Whether an agent loaded and followed AGENTS.md instructions is visible through the agent's own tracing mechanisms. Codex shows which instruction files it loaded in its session context. GitHub Copilot logs indicate AGENTS.md consumption. But the standard itself provides no tracing hooks.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: production_ready — AGENTS.md is deployed in production across 60,000+ open-source projects. It is consumed by enterprise-grade agents (GitHub Copilot, Google Jules, OpenAI Codex). The standard is stable, simple, and mature enough for production use. However, the lack of formal versioning and the absence of a formal specification (beyond the Markdown convention) mean that different agents may interpret the same file differently, which can lead to inconsistent behavior.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: 17,123 stars (agentsmd/agents.md repository, as of February 9, 2026). 1,207 forks. 112 open issues. Originally hosted under openai/agents.md, transferred to the agentsmd GitHub organization under AAIF governance.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: 60,000+ open-source projects have adopted AGENTS.md files (per OpenAI's AAIF announcement, December 2025). GitHub's blog analyzed 2,500+ repositories with AGENTS.md files as of November 2025. OpenAI's own Codex repository contains 88 AGENTS.md files. Supported by 20+ AI coding agents including: OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Devin, Factory, Gemini CLI, Google Jules, Android Studio (Gemini), Aider, Amp, Windsurf, RooCode, Kilo Code, goose, opencode, Zed, Warp, VS Code extensions, UiPath Autopilot, Semgrep, Phoenix.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: open-source — Completely free. MIT licensed. No paid tiers, no premium features, no enterprise edition. The standard is a Markdown file convention — there is nothing to monetize. Some third-party services offer AGENTS.md generation/optimization tools, but the standard itself is and will remain free.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: Software development workflow standardization — ensuring AI coding agents follow project conventions. CI/CD integration — documenting build, test, and deployment commands for autonomous agents. Monorepo management — providing package-level guidance in large codebases. Code review automation — defining PR standards and review criteria for agent-generated code. Onboarding — accelerating agent (and human) onboarding to new projects by centralizing institutional knowledge. Security guardrails — documenting forbidden actions and required safety checks. Open-source project maintenance — enabling external contributors' AI agents to work correctly on unfamiliar codebases.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Dominant standard for project-specific agent instructions. AGENTS.md faces limited competition: (1) CLAUDE.md (Anthropic) — proprietary equivalent for Claude Code only, not cross-tool portable, (2) .github/copilot-instructions.md — GitHub-specific, narrower scope, (3) .cursorrules / .cursor/rules — Cursor-specific configuration, (4) AGENT.md (singular, community alternative) — much less adopted. AGENTS.md's key advantage is portability: one file works across 20+ agents. Its donation to the AAIF under the Linux Foundation cements vendor-neutral governance. The GitHub Copilot team's endorsement (blog post analyzing 2,500+ repos, August 2025 support announcement) validates AGENTS.md as the cross-ecosystem winner.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: Not applicable as a standard — AGENTS.md can instruct agents to operate at any point on the autonomy spectrum. A file might say 'always ask before deleting files' (assistant mode) or 'run the full test suite and fix all failures autonomously' (autonomous mode). The standard is a communication channel between humans and agents, not an autonomy controller.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: AGENTS.md defines handoff expectations in prose. Common patterns include: 'if you encounter a failing test you cannot fix, create a GitHub Issue and stop', 'for security-sensitive changes, open a draft PR for human review', 'never deploy without explicit approval'. The actual handoff implementation depends on the consuming agent. AGENTS.md serves as the contract that both the agent and the human developer agree to.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Indirect — AGENTS.md improves over time through human editing based on observed agent behavior. Developers update the file when agents make mistakes (adding new constraints), discover better workflows, or onboard new team members. The feedback loop is: (1) agent misinterprets codebase → (2) human observes incorrect behavior → (3) human updates AGENTS.md with clearer instructions → (4) agent performs better next session. Git history tracks this evolution. No automated feedback mechanism exists in the standard.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: AGENTS.md is a zero-cost, high-impact productivity tool that every startup using AI coding agents should adopt immediately. USE AGENTS.md WHEN: (1) Your team uses any AI coding agent (Copilot, Cursor, Codex, etc.) — AGENTS.md ensures consistent behavior across all developers' agents, (2) You have more than one developer — it serves as machine-readable institutional knowledge that prevents agents from guessing conventions, (3) You maintain an open-source project — contributors' AI agents will work correctly on your codebase, (4) You are onboarding developers frequently — AGENTS.md accelerates both human and AI onboarding, (5) You want to future-proof your codebase — as more coding work shifts to agents, having clear AGENTS.md files becomes as important as having clear README files. WHEN TO INVEST MORE: (1) Monorepos with multiple packages — hierarchical AGENTS.md files prevent cross-package confusion, (2) Complex build systems — document every step so agents do not guess, (3) Regulated industries — use AGENTS.md to enforce compliance-relevant constraints. COST-BENEFIT: Creating an AGENTS.md file takes 30-60 minutes; the payoff is every subsequent AI-assisted coding session being more accurate and less error-prone. GitHub's analysis shows dramatic quality improvements in repositories with well-crafted AGENTS.md files. STRATEGIC NOTE: Understanding AGENTS.md and the broader AAIF ecosystem (MCP, A2A, goose) helps founders make informed decisions about AI tooling infrastructure.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: Nothing to build or buy — AGENTS.md is a free, open convention. The decision is whether to invest time in creating and maintaining a high-quality AGENTS.md file. The answer is almost always yes for any team using AI coding agents. Time investment: 30-60 minutes for initial creation, 5-10 minutes per update. Some teams use AI to generate an initial AGENTS.md from existing documentation and then refine it. Third-party AGENTS.md generators exist but are unnecessary for most projects — the format is intentionally simple.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 3 (AI project framing) — AGENTS.md as a practical tool for managing AI-assisted development workflows, part of the 'how to work with AI coding agents' toolkit alongside MCP and A2A. Demonstrates the Build vs Buy framework: zero-cost standard that dramatically improves agent reliability. Session 5 (ethics and governance) — AGENTS.md as an example of open standards governance (AAIF under Linux Foundation), security considerations (prompt injection via malicious AGENTS.md files), and the broader question of how humans maintain control over AI agents through documented instructions.

The standard is well-documented despite its simplicity.

confidence.caveats: AGENTS.md is evolving rapidly with no formal versioning — different agents may interpret the same file differently. Claude Code (Anthropic) does not natively support AGENTS.md, using CLAUDE.md instead, which is a notable gap in cross-tool portability. The 60,000+ adoption figure comes from OpenAI's December 2025 AAIF announcement and may not reflect active, well-maintained AGENTS.md files. Security concerns around prompt injection via malicious AGENTS.md files are an active area of discussion. The standard has no enforcement mechanism — it is advisory, not prescriptive. The v1.1 proposal (GitHub Issue #135) suggests the community recognizes the need for more formalization.
